caption: : RL training data statistic

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of training data samples across five distinct categories used in the reinforcement learning (RL) training process for the SRPO framework, as described in the paper “Enhancing Multimodal LLM Reasoning via Reflection-Aware Reinforcement Learning.” The horizontal axis lists the categories—“Other Math,” “Geometric Math,” “Charts Diagrams,” “Natural Science,” and “General Reasoning”—arranged in descending order of sample count. The vertical axis, labeled “Number of Samples,” ranges from 0 to 14,000 with major gridlines at intervals of 2,000, using a linear scale. Each category is represented by a single solid orange bar with its exact sample count labeled above: “Other Math” has 14,333 samples, “Geometric Math” has 10,227, “Charts Diagrams” has 5,953, “Natural Science” has 3,343, and “General Reasoning” has 3,534. The chart visually emphasizes the disparity in sample sizes, with “Other Math” having the highest count and “Natural Science” the lowest among the five, while “General Reasoning” slightly exceeds “Natural Science.” No additional visual encoding such as color differentiation or grouping is present, and all bars are uniformly styled.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of training samples across five distinct categories used in the RL training data for the SRPO framework, as described in the paper “SRPO: Enhancing Multimodal LLM Reasoning via Reflection-Aware Reinforcement Learning.” The vertical axis, labeled “Number of Samples,” ranges from 0 to 14,000 with tick marks at intervals of 2,000, and uses a linear scale. The horizontal axis lists the five categories: “Other Math,” “Geometric Math,” “Charts Diagrams,” “Natural Science,” and “General Reasoning,” arranged from left to right in descending order of sample count. Each category is represented by a single solid orange bar with its exact sample count labeled above it. “Other Math” has the highest number of samples at 14,333, followed by “Geometric Math” at 10,227, “Charts Diagrams” at 5,953, “General Reasoning” at 3,534, and “Natural Science” at 3,343. The bars are uniformly colored and unstacked, with no additional visual emphasis or grouping, and the chart includes a light gray grid to aid in value estimation.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm stellt die Verteilung der Stichprobenanzahl für verschiedene Kategorien von Trainingsdaten im Rahmen des RL-Trainings dar, wie im Kontext des Papiers „SRPO: Enhancing Multimodal LLM Reasoning via Reflection-Aware Reinforcement Learning“ beschrieben. Auf der vertikalen Achse ist die „Number of Samples“ (Anzahl der Stichproben) auf einer linearen Skala von 0 bis 14.000 dargestellt, mit Tick-Markierungen in 2.000er-Schritten. Die horizontale Achse listet fünf Kategorien auf: „Other Math“, „Geometric Math“, „Charts Diagrams“, „Natural Science“ und „General Reasoning“, in dieser Reihenfolge von links nach rechts. Jeder Balken ist in einheitlichem orangefarbenem Farbton gehalten und trägt oben die genaue Stichprobenanzahl als numerischen Wert. Der Balken für „Other Math“ ist der höchste mit 14.333 Stichproben, gefolgt von „Geometric Math“ mit 10.227, „Charts Diagrams“ mit 5.953, „Natural Science“ mit 3.343 und „General Reasoning“ mit 3.534. Die Balken sind nicht nach Höhe sortiert, sondern in der gegebenen Kategorienreihenfolge angeordnet; es gibt keine visuellen Hervorhebungen wie Schattierungen oder Umrandungen, und alle Balken sind gleichmäßig gestaltet, wobei die Höhe direkt proportional zur Stichprobenanzahl ist.
